source_refs.note: Topic 2.2.1, printed page 25: Table 2.2 of particle properties, with Quick Check 2.1 as the self-check.

blocks.text: The three fundamental particles of the atom, the electron, proton and neutron, have the charges and masses given in Table 2.2.

blocks.caption: Properties of the three fundamental particles (Table 2.2)

blocks.prompt: Using the table, show why the mass of an atom is almost entirely in its nucleus.
blocks.explanation: A proton or neutron has a mass of about 1 amu, while an electron has 5.4858 x 10^-4 amu, about 1/1836 as much. Even an atom with many electrons therefore carries almost all its mass in the protons and neutrons of the nucleus.

items: Proton +1, about 1.0073 amu; neutron 0, 1.0087 amu; electron -1, 5.4858 x 10^-4 amu; the unit charge is 1.6022 x 10^-19 coulomb.
